title: Predictive capacity bump and graceful-drop policy for embeddings
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: High-variance tenant traffic for the embeddings endpoint causes repeated cold autoscale events and elevated p99 latencies. Current autoscaler reacts to queue length and CPU/GPU utilization but is often too slow for bursty patterns; when capacity lags we either (a) allow long tails, or (b) drop requests abruptly. Both lead to poor customer experience and unpredictable unit economics.

Objective: Add a predictive 'capacity bump' layer plus a graceful admission/drop policy that: (1) proactively spins up headroom when early indicators suggest an imminent burst; (2) applies prioritized, latency-first admission with progressive graceful-drop tiers instead of binary throttles; (3) integrates with billing/quotas to avoid surprising costs.

Scope: hosted embeddings router and Dedicated autoscaler path. No changes to model runtime kernels in this ticket — just routing/autoscale/admission logic and observability.

Outcomes: reduce p99 inference latency for top 50 tenants during bursts by at least 30%, reduce abrupt error spikes (5xx/429) from sudden scale events by 70%, and lower average cold-start frequency by 50% in the staging traffic generator tests.
acceptance_criteria: Staging load generator demonstrates predictive bump reduces cold-starts by >=50% across 10 representative tenant profiles
P99 latency for top-50 tenants during synthetic bursts improves >=30% in staging compared to baseline run
System exposes metrics for bump triggers, bump duration, and graceful-drop decisions in Console dashboard
No increase in sustained overprovision cost beyond a configurable long-window budget (default 10%)
Feature toggles exist: predictive-bump enabled flag, graceful-drop policy selector, per-tenant override
implementation_notes: Add predictive signal processor in the router: input features = short-window QPS slope, queue length gradient, recent tenant burst history (last 15m), and request size distribution
Implement lightweight ML heuristic (exponential moving average + slope threshold) as v1; avoid heavy models to keep reliability and explainability
Autoscaler API change: accept 'headroom_reservation' request to pre-warm N instances for a tenant group; defaults governed by a global policy

Admission controller: implement three-tier graceful-drop — (1) soft-defer with priority retry window (HTTP 202 + Retry-After), (2) partial degradation (reduce batching window / switch to lower-quality quantized model), (3) final throttling (429) — choose based on tenant SLA and request priority
Quota integration: when bump would exceed committed reserved capacity for Dedicated, consult tenant commitment and fallback to lowest-latency feasible option (partial degradation) instead of bumping
Configuration: per-tenant profile includes 'burst_tolerance', 'preferred_degradation', and 'predictive_enabled' flags stored in config service
Expose feature flag to roll out in three stages: Canary tenants (5), org-level beta (20), full rollout
Instrument end-to-end traces for bump lifecycle (trigger->prewarm->serve->teardown) and track cost impact by token count and GPU-hours
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge router predictive signal processor behind feature flag; run in monitoring-only mode (no prewarm) to collect false-positive/negative rates
Week 2: Enable headroom_reservation API and dry-run prewarm (allocate reserved instances but mark them as 'monitor-only' so they don't serve requests) to measure provisioning latency
Week 3: Canary enable predictive bump for 5 low-risk tenants; enable soft-defer graceful-drop behavior for these tenants
Week 4: Expand to 20 tenants and enable partial degradation fallback for Dedicated contracts; run cost-sensitivity tests
Week 5: Full rollout with automatic budget enforcement and per-tenant opt-out; monitor 72h closely and revert knob if error rates or costs exceed thresholds
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards to create: predictive-bump-overview, bump-trigger-latency, graceful-drop-incidents, per-tenant-bump-cost
SLOs: bump false-positive rate < 15%, bump provisioning success within target latency (cold->warm) 95th pct < 30s, graceful-drop-induced error fraction < 5% of normal traffic
Alerts: ramp-up if bump-trigger rate spikes > 3x baseline in 10m, if 429s due to graceful-drop exceed 0.5% of total traffic for a tenant in 5m, if prewarm cost accrual exceeds configured budget
Runbook steps: rollback flags -> disable predictive bump -> revert to baseline autoscaler; if rollback fails, scale manual capacity via Dedicated console and notify EngOps
Playbook for customer-impact incidents: label incident as 'graceful-drop' if partial degradation applied, gather trace IDs and sample requests, notify impacted accounts and open follow-up ticket
